en: Title: Mahādhāraṇī Source: Hidas & Szántó, CUL Add. 1680.8 Tibetan: D 529 = 888

[29] Homage to the Blessed Noble Mahādhāraṇī! Thus have I heard: at one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Śrāvastī, in the Jeta Grove, in Anāthapiṇḍada’s monastery, together with a great saṅgha of monks, numbering twelve hundred and fifty monks. Now, the Venerable Ānanda, having completed the rains retreat at Sāketa, took his bowl and robe and approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he bowed his head at the feet of the Blessed One and stood to one side. As the Venerable Ānanda was standing to one side, the Blessed One said this to him:

"Take up, Ānanda, these words of the great dhāraṇī-mantra for the sake, benefit, and happiness of all sentient beings; uphold them! Grasp them! Recite them! Attend to them in your mind! Master them! Why is that? Because, Ānanda, these words of the great dhāraṇī-mantra are difficult to encounter. The appearance of Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksambuddhas in the world is rare, just like the flower of the Udumbara tree."

"Ānanda, whichever son of good family or daughter of good family shall uphold, recite, cause others to grasp, attend to, and master these words of the great dhāraṇī-mantra, they shall not meet their end by means of a weapon; they shall not meet their end by poison or fire; nor shall they have any fear of kings."

Neither gods, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, pretas, piśācas, bhūtas, kumbhāṇḍas, pūtanās, kaṭapūtanas, lūtās, apasmāras, unmādas, kṛtyakas, nor any other malevolent spirits, nor planets or stars, shall cause him harm. Nor shall he suffer from fevers—whether those occurring every day, every two days, every three days, every four days, those arising from the combination of humors (sāṃnipātika), chronic fevers, or irregular fevers. Nor shall he be afflicted by [other ailments], nor shall there be any root-rites (mūlakarma) directed against him.
Namely: *Bale mahābale | jvale mahājvale | jvalite | ukke mukke | sampade mahāsampade | tapane mahātapane svāhā*.
Indeed, Ānanda, these mantra-words of the great dhāraṇī were spoken by seventy-seven koṭis of perfectly awakened ones, and they have now been spoken by me as well.

"Ānanda, any son of good family or daughter of good family who shall uphold, recite, cause others to grasp, attend to, and master these words of the great dhāraṇī-mantra will remember their births for seven lifetimes, and their thought of awakening (bodhicitta) shall not become deluded.
It is as follows: aṇḍe maṇḍe | kṣame | mahākṣame | varado | anado | kule | [+++++++++++saha] svāhā."
"Ānanda, these are indeed the words of the great dhāraṇī-mantra. They have been spoken by eighty-eight koṭis of perfectly awakened Buddhas, and they are spoken by me now as well.

Any son of good family or daughter of good family, Ānanda, who shall uphold, cause others to uphold, recite, attend to, and master these words of the dhāraṇī-mantra, will remember their births for fourteen lifetimes, and their thought of awakening (bodhicitta) shall not become deluded."

Namely as follows: *aṭṭe*, *vaṭe*, *ṭhakke*, *ṭharakke*, *ṭake*, *vare varavarakoṣi*, *mahākoṣi*, *ili mili raurave*, *mahāraurave timi*, *bhūtaṅgame*, *mahābhūtaṅgame*, *parāyaṇe*, *ghasi*, *mahāmāti*, *ghasi svāhā*.
Indeed, Ānanda, these mantra-words of the great dhāraṇī have been spoken by ninety-nine koṭis of perfectly awakened Buddhas; they have also been spoken by me now.

"Ānanda, whichever son of good family or daughter of good family shall uphold, recite, cause others to grasp, attend to, and master these dhāraṇī mantra-words, he or she will remember their births for twenty-one lifetimes, and their thought of awakening (bodhicitta) shall not become deluded.
It is as follows: akkile | vakkile | rule | auhani | mohani | stambhani | jambhani | svāhā."

Indeed, Ānanda, by means of these great dhāraṇī mantra-words, even for a withered tree, having performed a rite of peace and well-being, one should bind it with this protective amulet (*pratisara*) so that there is an avoidance of punishment; leaves shall grow upon it, and sprouts, shoots, flowers, and fruits shall also grow. What need is there to speak, then, of a human body endowed with consciousness? With the exception, Ānanda, of the ripening of past karma.

"Even so, Ānanda, even the sun and moon, possessing such great supernormal power and such great majesty, might fall to the ground; even so, Ānanda, this great earth might suddenly shake; even so, Ānanda, the four great oceans, so deep and so vast, might dry up; even so, Ānanda, Sumeru, the king of mountains, might be moved from its place—and yet, this [the Tathāgata’s word] could not be otherwise."

Ānanda, whoever—whether a god, a nāga, an asura, a garuḍa, a kiṃnara, a mahoraga, a yakṣa, a rākṣasa, a kumbhāṇḍa, a pūtana, a kaṭapūtana, a bhūta, an apasmāra, a human, or a non-human—should transgress these great dhāraṇī-mantra words, against him King Dhṛtarāṣṭra shall strike with a wheel made of heated iron, and Vajrapāṇi, the great general of the yakṣas, shall strike with a wheel that is blazing, aflame, fully ignited, and become a single mass of fire. Śakra, the lord of the gods, [shall strike] with [a wheel] that is blazing... becoming a single mass of fire. Furthermore, not even a drop of water from his alms-bowl shall fall upon the royal capital Āḍakavatī; rather, his head shall split into seven pieces like the cluster of blossoms on an arjaka tree.
Thus spoke the Blessed One; and the Venerable Ānanda, those monks, and the world with its gods, humans, asuras, garuḍas, and gandharvas, rejoiced in the words of the Blessed One.
The Noble Great Dhāraṇī is completed.
